dashboards.description: A set of basic check that focuses on the big picture. You should be able to pass these health check. Do this check at least daily each morning.

config.description: A big drop in these numbers indicate a major issue.
config.title: KEY METRICS

config.description: Red or orange alerts means the issues need immediate attentions. It's not something you defer to the next day. Expect the numbers to be low, once you fine tune the alerts definition to your environment
config.title: URGENT ISSUES

config.description:
Since VM runs on ESXi, any availability or consumption issue at ESXi need to be checked.

The data comes from all ESXi in the environment.
config.title: AVAILABILITY

config.description:
Is your IaaS serving the VMs well? Each of the trend charts show the worst experience of any VM in your private cloud. A low number means all VMs are getting a good service from your shared infrastructure.

Aim for yellow to orange range, indicating you're pushing utilization hard but not sacrificing performance too much.
config.title: PERFORMANCE

config.description:
While you're bound to have large VM, they should be minimized as they can impact both capacity and performance.
The heat map shows the large VM. Each box represents a VM, grouped by vSphere Cluster so you can see where they are. The box size represents the relative vCPU configured size among the VM, while the color represents the configured. memory.
Pro Tip: configure the threshold
config.title: Monster VM

config.description:
The aggregate workload or demand on your private cloud should be fairly stable. If not, it should matches either the business cycle or data center activities. 

Investigate if the number drops when it's a supposed to be busy day for business, or if the number spike when it's supposed to be a quiet hours.
config.title: CAPACITY

config.description: Track all 7 changes to VM states: guest reboot, guest shutdown, VM power off, VM power on, VM reset, VM Standby Guest and VM Suspend.
config.title: VM: State Change

config.description:
Total SCSI commands (read or write) in the entire environment. 

Pro Tip: set a threshold so your expectation is known as a team.
config.title: Total Load: Disk IOPS

config.description:
While your private cloud is dynamic, the degree of changes need to be within your expectation. It needs to match business cycle or data center operations.

Investigate if the number drops when it's a supposed to be busy day for business, or if the number spike when it's supposed to be a quiet hours.
config.title: VOLATILITY

config.description: 7 types of VM inventory changes: clone, create, delete, reconfigure, register to vCenter, unregister to vCenter, deploy from template.
config.title: VM: Inventory Change

config.description: Red = attend as soon as possible, not delay until end of day. This number should be 0 most of the time.
config.title: Alerts: Urgent and Important

config.description:
Total network throughput (send and receive) in the entire environment. 

Pro Tip: set a threshold so your expectation is known as a team.
config.title: Total Load: Network Throughput

config.description: If these numbers change drastically and not matching your expectation, something wrong has happened.
config.title: Key Inventory

config.description: Total amount of reservation given to VM memory. This amount should be 0 as memory reservation is "sticky". It persists despite the Guest OS not using the page anymore.
config.title: Memory Reservation

config.description: Total amount of reservation given to VM CPU. This amount should be low or 0. Setting reservation impacts both vSphere DRS and HA, creating a risk of overall performance.
config.title: CPU Reservation

resourceKindMetrics.metricName: Number of VM Operations|State|VM Power Off
Number of VM Operations|State|VM Guest Reboot
Number of VM Operations|State|VM Guest Shutdown
Number of VM Operations|State|VM Standby Guest

config.description:
Tracks all 6 types, grouped into cold or hot migration.
compute change, storage change, both changes.
config.title: VM: Location Change

config.description:
The number should be low. It may not be 0.

Attend by end of day, not defer until tomorrow. Alerts that you defer until tomorrow means it's not urgent. It's more effective to see these non-urgent warning in totality as insight than as individual alerts
config.title: Alerts: Urgent but Not Important

dashboards.name: Overall Daily Check
